why_null: All four cases in the library were considered against the motif of usaid-deficit, and none matched at the structural threshold. B-01 (casualty-inflation cascade, May 2019) and B-03 (moral-shock acceleration, Aug 2025) both run on moral shock: a count of the dead or a video of a death moves people within hours, and the reasoning at issue concerns what happened to a body. This narrative carries no shock event and no count of persons; its spine is a budget magnitude followed by a lever priced as sufficient, so the shape does not repeat. B-02 (fabricated-provision cascade, Oct 2020) turns on provisions attributed to a statute whose final text was not yet public, an instrument read for content it did not carry. Nothing in this narrative reads an instrument at all. B-04 (scope-inflation panic, Jan 2025) is the nearest case in the library and still is not the same shape: there a regulation had already narrowed a rise to a listed set of goods and the telling widened it back across the whole consumption basket, so a written restriction existed and was stepped over. This narrative has no narrowing instrument available to widen. Its shape is a ratio asserted while neither of its terms is stated: the line's annual dollar outlay that a cut could free, and the size of the deficit against which any freeing would be measured. That is a sufficiency claim about a lever, not scope inflation. Shared subject matter with B-04 (public budgets, tax and spending, a share of a national total) is topic overlap, and topic overlap is expressly not the threshold. Blueprint D-15 permits silence, so silence is the answer here.
